task_instance: Create a minimal Expo Router app with API routes (app/api/hello+api.ts, app/api/users+api.ts), export the web bundle with `npx expo export -p web`, verify it locally with `npx expo serve` + curl, then deploy it to EAS Hosting with `eas login` / `eas deploy` as the skill's Deployment section describes.
blocker_detail: The skill's core stated deliverable is deploying the exported web app + API routes to EAS Hosting (Expo's paid, managed Cloudflare Workers service). `eas-cli` installs and runs fine (`npx eas-cli@latest whoami` -> 'Not logged in'), but proceeding requires `eas login` against an Expo account and then `eas deploy`, which is an account-bound, paid cloud service (per the skill's own banner: 'EAS service - costs apply'). That is explicitly forbidden by the sandbox rules (no credentials/account sign-in, no paid or account-bound services, no public deployment), so the actual EAS Hosting deployment step could not be attempted.
evidence: Everything short of the account-gated deploy step was built and verified end-to-end in /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/exec/expo__skills__eas-hosting/myapp: scaffolded an Expo SDK 57 app (`create-expo-app`), added expo-router (aligned to SDK 57 versions after a version-mismatch failure), created app/_layout.tsx, app/index.tsx, app/api/hello+api.ts (GET) and app/api/users+api.ts (GET/POST) exactly per the skill's examples, set app.json web.output='server'. Ran `EXPO_OFFLINE=1 npx expo export -p web` successfully (network to Expo's telemetry/compat-check host was blocked by the sandbox's outbound proxy with 'HTTP Proxy Network Error: Forbidden'; EXPO_OFFLINE=1 worked around that for the export step) producing dist/ with 'API routes (2): /api/hello, /api/users' and compiled functions under dist/server/_expo/functions/api/. Started `npx expo serve` (http://localhost:8081) and verified with curl: `curl http://localhost:8081/api/hello` -> {"message":"Hello from Expo!"}; `curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/api/users -d '{"name":"Test"}'` -> {"created":{"name":"Test"}}, status 201; and `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:8081/` -> 200. This confirms the free/open-source portion (authoring API routes, exporting the web bundle, testing locally) works fully in this runtime. Then ran `npx eas-cli@latest whoami`, which returned 'Not logged in' -- confirming the deploy step needs an Expo account/credentials and is a paid service, which the safety rules prohibit, so the actual 'deploy to EAS Hosting' deliverable was not attempted or achieved.
